daily.title: North Korea fires around 10 ballistic missiles into sea
daily.summary: The latest ballistic missile launch comes amid rising border tensions with South Korea and uncertainty over potential nuclear talks with the US.

daily.title: US: Department of Homeland Security data leak exposes details of more than 40,000 employees
daily.summary: The leaked information reportedly includes names, phone numbers and email addresses of personnel across several US security agencies. This follows recent data breaches involving the FBI and the Defense Department.

daily.title: EU countries block Canada's 'associate membership' plan
daily.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wanted to give Canada a special status within the EU. But Germany and other member states have raised objections ahead of a summit in Montreal.

daily.title: Flavio Bolsonaro lands in US, declares himself 'leader' of Brazil
daily.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro declared himself the rightful leader of his country despite losing the presidential election runoff on Sunday. He and his family have fled to the US.

daily.title: How do the US midterms work, and why are they so important for Trump's presidency?
daily.summary: US voters are electing a new Congress. The results will be decisive for the future of the United States, and a judgment on Donald Trump's second term as president.

daily.title: Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
daily.summary: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

daily.title: One year on, families seek justice after election violence
daily.summary: One year after Tanzania's deadly post-election violence, families are still seeking answers. A government inquiry recorded 518 deaths. DW research has documented apparent use of excessive force by security forces.

daily.title: What would a new Israeli government mean for Arab neighbors? More of the same is expected, with some small positives predicted.
daily.summary: A new Israeli government is unlikely to bring big changes on controversial topics like Palestinian statehood and Israeli troops in Lebanon and Syria, experts say. Some small positives may be possible though.

daily.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy irked by US-Russia-China summit
daily.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy has voiced his concerns about a probable meeting between the leaders of the US, China and Russia next month. Plus, a localized truce appeared to be holding in the town of Oleshky.

daily.title: Spanish train crash leaves 68 dead, PM Sanchez declares 3 days of mourning
daily.summary: Two high-speed trains carrying hundreds of passengers collided south of Madrid. Spain's transport minister said one of the trains was told to continue its journey despite a "red signal" being in effect.

daily.title: Is Iran headed to war or peace after Mecca alliance meeting?
daily.summary: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey have taken their latest peace push directly to Tehran. Officially, it was to avert a new military escalation, but their diplomatic outreach can also be seen as a warning to Iran.

daily.title: Gen Z protests in Germany: Is France-style violence looming?
daily.summary: Young people in Germany will take to the streets this weekend to demand education and action on climate change. Politicians warn that the protests could become violent, as in France, but the situations are different.

daily.title: Israel election: Netanyahu-led bloc in slight lead with more than 80% of votes counted
daily.summary: While partial results show the pro-Netanyahu bloc ahead of the anti-Netanyahu bloc, the final tally could take days. Neither grouping is expected to win a majority, with tough coalition talks ahead. Follow DW.

daily.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
daily.summary: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

daily.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
daily.summary: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

daily.title: Germany news: Parties debate who should succeed President Steinmeier, with several women under discussion
daily.summary: Germany's political parties are weighing possible successors to President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, with no candidate agreed yet. Meanwhile, a poll suggests most Germans are giving Halloween a miss this year.

daily.title: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
daily.summary: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

daily.title: Dozens of people killed after high-speed trains collide in central Spain
daily.summary: At least 68 people have been killed in a train crash in central Spain, local authorities have confirmed. Rail services between Madrid and Seville have been suspended.

daily.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
daily.summary: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

daily.title: Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
daily.summary: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

weekly.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
weekly.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

weekly.title: Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive
weekly.summary: During a visit to Singapore, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Germany want to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.

weekly.title: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
weekly.summary: The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

weekly.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
weekly.summary: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.

weekly.title: Steinmeier in China: A major state visit in uncertain times
weekly.summary: President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is traveling to China on a state visit in a period of political and economic uncertainty. Germany is seeking alternative partners in the region but also wants good ties with Beijing.

weekly.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
weekly.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But ahead of the US midterm elections, does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

weekly.title: France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
weekly.summary: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

weekly.title: Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
weekly.summary: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

weekly.title: In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
weekly.summary: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

weekly.title: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
weekly.summary: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

weekly.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
weekly.summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

weekly.title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
weekly.summary: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

weekly.title: Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
weekly.summary: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

weekly.title: Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament
weekly.summary: After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.

weekly.title: Germany sit out FIFA Under-15 World Cup as Russia return
weekly.summary: Germany is one a handful of FIFA's 211 nations to refuse an invitation to play at the inaugural Under-15 World Cup. The tournament will also mark Russia's return to the FIFA fold.

weekly.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
weekly.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

weekly.title: Serbia: Tens of thousands rally ahead of elections
weekly.summary: After two years of student-led protests, Serbia will soon vote in what observers describe as a referendum-like snap election pitting strongman Aleksandar Vucic against the student movement.

weekly.title: Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
weekly.summary: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.

weekly.title: Are the French police the most violent in the EU?
weekly.summary: As protests continue in France, the French police are under scrutiny after new allegations of police brutality. The force has a bigger arsenal than most in Europe.

weekly.title: Ukraine: Life near the front line in Sloviansk
weekly.summary: As Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, thousands of residents refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out. For many, poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation painfully difficult.

weekly.title: Can Germany revive its economy before the far-right AfD gains ground?
weekly.summary: Conflicts, rising costs and Chinese competition are testing Germany's economic model like never before. Can new growth sectors create jobs and ease voters' economic fears, thereby helping contain the far-right AfD?

weekly.title: Bulgaria: Concerns about security in the Black Sea dominate presidential election campaign
weekly.summary: Bulgaria's presidential election campaign has been shaped by recent drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea and the government's reduced support for Ukraine, making foreign policy a key factor in the first round.

developing.title: Live: Fresh protests hit France amid heightened security
developing.summary: Police and elite security forces are out in force in French cities as thousands participate in a new round of protests. The protest location was changed last minute in Paris. Follow DW.

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
